# v1.9.2 — Stop the queue watchdog crying wolf during long lyrics passes

A single-issue follow-up to v1.9.1. Anyone who saw the amber **⚠ Watchdog: no progress signal for 10 min — item may be stuck. Will auto-fail after 20 min total.** entry pop up during companion lyrics conversion (or any other long activity-log-only enrichment pass) on a multi-thousand-track library should upgrade.

## What's fixed

- **Queue watchdog no longer false-positives on long activity-log-only passes (#846).** The watchdog detects stalled queue items by snapshotting a tuple of `progress / processing_progress / processing_label / current_track / completed_tracks` fields every 60 seconds and warning if the tuple goes bit-identical for 10 minutes. During the once-per-item companion lyrics conversion v1.9.1 introduced via #843 — which fires hundreds of `Companion: converted N TTML file(s) to Enhanced LRC` activity-log lines but doesn't touch any of those fields — the watchdog mistook the absence of label/progress changes for a stall and emitted the WARN even though the conversion was actively making progress. v1.9.2 adds a per-download activity-event counter that bumps from inside `emit_inner` (every `emit_download_log` / warn / error / verbose call) and `emit_subprocess_line` (every GAMDL stdout/stderr line). The watchdog snapshot now includes that counter, so any activity-log emission for the item changes the snapshot and resets the stall timer. The behaviour for **genuinely** stuck items — no activity-log events at all for 10+ min, the case v1.7.0's external watchdog (#818) was added to catch — is unchanged.

## Notes

- **1 new unit test** in `services::queue_watchdog::tests`: `snapshot_picks_up_activity_count_change` confirms the counter participates in the snapshot's `PartialEq`. All 1,189 backend tests pass.
- **No behaviour change for system-level activity-log events.** `emit_app_log` (rendered with the `[System]` chip) deliberately does NOT bump any per-download counter — those events aren't tied to a specific stalled item and shouldn't influence per-item stall detection.
- **Memory cost is negligible.** The per-download counter map grows by one `u64` per ever-seen download_id — 10,000 downloads is ~240 KB. Cleanup on terminal-state would be possible but isn't worth the complexity.
